text:
alex: Quick report: sample-app stalls during large list export when client-side throttling + cursor pagination enabled. No crash, just huge lag then many 429s. Anyone seen this?

mona: which SDK/version and config?

alex: python-sdk 0.7.3, config: throttler.window=120, throttler.adaptive=true, pagination.cursor=true, pagination.eager=true.

kevin: two suspects: 1) eager cursor prefetch causes cascade of requests, 2) auth refresh not coalesced so retries multiply.

alex: logs show inflight hit limit, queued grows, then auth refresh kicks in and we get duplicate sends.

mona: short fixes: set pagination.eager=false or reduce window and max_inflight. Also centralize token refresh with a promise/future so only one refresh runs.

kevin: SDK parity note: go and js SDKs already expose refreshLock helper; python missing it. Filing a parity issue.

ops-bot: Created issue #5057: python-sdk auth.refresh_lock parity + inflight decrement reorder.

tara: another DX item: sample-app README should warn about "eager pagination + adaptive throttling" and suggest safe defaults (initial window 40, max_inflight 6, prefetch_delay 100ms).

alex: thanks — applying prefetch_delay + refresh lock locally fixed it. Leaving thread for follow-up after PR lands.
